CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath. She reports experiencing dyspnea and palpitations with mild exercise or walking, such as walking up her driveway. She notes this is happening more frequently lately. She has recently increased her exercise regimen to lose weight. She wonders if her chronic back pain may be contributing to these symptoms. She reports smoking approximately once per day, down from two packs per day at her last visit. Pulmonary function tests show possible asthma or COPD. Chest x-ray demonstrates a flattened diaphragm, consistent with COPD. Physical examination reveals mild wheezes in all lung fields.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any other issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression
Smoking history
Chronic back pain

MEDICATIONS
Effexor for depression
Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports smoking approximately once per day, reduced from two packs per day previously. She is exercising more recently to lose weight gained during COVID.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: No acute distress noted. Lungs: Mild wheezes present in all lung fields. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests: Consistent with possible asthma or COPD.
Chest x-ray: Flattened diaphragm noted, consistent with COPD.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
COPD (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease): Diagnosed based on pulmonary function tests, chest x-ray findings, and clinical presentation. Started on Combivent two puffs twice daily. Prescribed Albuterol two puffs as needed for shortness of breath. Prescribed Prednisone taper pack. Continue smoking cessation efforts.
Depression: Stable on current Effexor regimen. Continue current medication. Patient counseled to do yoga for depression and back pain management.
Chronic back pain: Continue Gabapentin (Neurontin). Recommend yoga.
